title: perf(canary): auto-detect KV-cache-induced regressions + hysteresis rollout guard
author: Samir Kapoor
release_notes: Add automated detection for KV-cache-related latency regressions and a hysteresis-based rollout guard to prevent flappy canary rollouts. Backfilled tests and observability dashboards. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Context: We've seen intermittent canary regressions that correlate with KV cache eviction/flush behavior under certain prefix distributions. These regressions can be short-lived and cause canary rollouts to flip/flop leading to noisy rollbacks. This PR introduces automated detection logic that attributes latency spikes to KV-cache events and a hysteresis rollout guard to avoid reacting to transient spikes.

What this change does: - Adds a KV-cache anomaly detector that consumes canary latency and cache eviction metrics and identifies likely cache-induced regressions using a small heuristic (latency correlation with eviction_rate and kv_cache_miss_ratio). - Adds hysteresis state machine to the perf canary controller: canary must exceed the configured regression threshold for N consecutive evaluation windows before an automatic rollback is triggered; similarly, recovery requires M consecutive clean windows. Defaults are conservative (N=3, M=5) and configurable via the perf-canary config. - Emits structured diagnostics (canary_regression_reason="kv-cache-eviction" with contributing metrics) to tracing and canary audit events to help root-cause. - Adds end-to-end tests that simulate KV cache churn and assert the detector attributes regressions correctly and that the hysteresis prevents flappy rollouts. - Updates docs and runbooks describing how to tune thresholds and evaluate false positives.

Motivation: Short flaky rollbacks erode confidence in automated rollouts and create noisy incident signals. Identifying common, actionable root causes (like KV cache churn) and gating the rollback with a small hysteresis window buys time for transient events to settle while still enabling automated protection for true regressions.

Risk: Low. Changes are limited to the perf canary controller and the detector; default thresholds are conservative and feature is behind a config flag in perf-canary values. Unit/integration/e2e perf tests added to validate behavior.

Testing: - Unit tests for detector heuristics and state machine (services/serving/perf/canary/tests/test_detector.py) - Integration test that wires a synthetic KV-cache churn generator into the canary evaluator and asserts no rollback for transient spikes, rollback for sustained regressions. - CI perf job run against a small cluster (passed).

Related: ENG-2314 (perf canary roadmap), SUP-4421 (customer incident that motivated this).
